Letters of Insurgents is an awesome book, and I implore you to read it. You can read it online, download the audiobook, or at amazon. A summary from AKPress is pasted below.

Yarostan and Sophia work in a factory in eastern Europe. They live, argue, and take action. The workers rebel, a general strike, an armed uprising, They rule at the streets and in the factory, argue about the future, for a moment the world belongs to them. But soon there is a new government, a workers government, a new army, a red army. Insurgent workers are being whipped back to the factory, the workers government puts workers in jail and up against the wall. Sophia escapes to a western country, Yarostan has to spend years in prison. Both in the eastern workers state and in the western democracy people find ways to survive, to relate to friends and enemies, and are forced to work for others.

After a quarter of a century without a word, Sophia receives a letter from Yarostan. They start corresponding. About their new lives, new and old friends and comrades, work, politics and the struggle against work and politics. It’s about history, memories, hope, and experience. Nothing is taken for granted; everything is questioned. Was it really the workers government, the red army or something else from outside that crushed the revolution? Did the union and the party deceit, or did the union and the party win? Why did we go back to the factory? Do we need the factory? Can we really blame anyone other than ourselves? What is holding us back?

I didn't have a whole lot of expectations going into this race. My training for the past several months hasn't been all I have wanted it to be. I was going to be happy with just meeting my previous performance from 2013 (Swim: 1:15, Bike, 6:05, Run: 4:53, Total: 12:25:57). I also wanted to break 6 hours for my bike split. Other than that I had no expectations.

Prep:

Nothing super eventful to say here. I got up to Windsor on Friday and did packet pickup uneventfully. Then I got some food, checked into my hotel and tuned up the bike. Was in bed by 8PM. I like to get to the start early so that I'm not in a rush. I managed to get to the start around 5 AM and had plenty of time to double and triple check everything before 6:30 AM swim start.

Swim(1:22): https://www.strava.com/activities/354730729

I suck at swimming and when you consider that I haven't been in the pool in months I think this is about what I would expect. A little slower than last time but not too bad. Nothing I can't make up later. Swim was pretty easy as usual for Vineman. The river is very slow moving and super shallow. Lots of sections you can stand up and walk if necessary. At the turnaround point on the course you really can't swim and are forced to walk. Nothing super eventful here.

T1:

Took this pretty easy. With my low expectations I saw no reason to rush this part. Best to make sure I do everything properly.

Bike(5:46): https://www.strava.com/activities/354731037

Pretty happy with the bike. Weather was nice the entire time. The beginning wasn't too cold and it stayed reasonable during the middle of the day. I often having issue with my feet getting really cold in the beginning of the bike but this wasn't an issue today. For the first 2/3 of the course I was paying a lot of attention to my power and trying to force myself to slow down. I used bestbikesplit to estimate the necessary power for a 6 hour bike split. I was aiming for 150-155 average power. I ended up closer to 165 W but also with a faster time. Around 80 miles into the course I started really hurting and considering slacking off. The heat was getting to me and my legs felt like they had nothing left. Also my neck started getting really sore and I had trouble staying on the aero bars. After muscling it up chalk hill for the second time around 100-105 miles I started feeling better. The back half of the course is pretty fast and I pushed through to T2. Pretty happy with the bike performance as I took 14 minutes off my target 6 hours. Also, I gained back the time compared to my 2013 performance that I had lost on the swim.

T2:

See T1.

Run (4:30): https://www.strava.com/activities/354730892

At the start of the run I look at my watch and did some quick estimates in my head to compare how I was doing with 2013. My barely functioning brain determined that I could safely run a 5 hour marathon and get a PR. I kept this in my head the entire course. I figured with no walking this should be very possible. I hit the porta potty once at around mile 5. I paced myself well on fluids for the bike so I didn't make any stops. I didn't want to carry around more fluids than necessary. For the first two laps I was primarily focused on keeping myself cool. I took a lot of ice and was doing a combination of putting it in my hat, in my trisuit and chewing on it. Other than that I had mostly water and grapes. I love grapes because you can grab a handful of them and munch on them in between aid stations. Around half way I started grabbing coke to keep everything going. When I started the third lap I realized exactly how well I was doing and started to target a sub 12 hour finish which would be a 4:40 marathon. For the final lap I kept chipping off time and moving below 12 hours.

Overall(11:50:56):

Quite happy with this performance. A 35 minute PR is always great especially considering that I had no expectations at the start of the race. 11:30 for IM Wisconsin?

Teams outside Power Five face difficult odds to reach College Football Playoff

Having a panel like the playoff committee can only help non-P5 schools (G5, mid majors, "great 5", whatever you want to call them) because they will take the whole body of work into consideration. Taking BSU as an example, they lost two key players over the summer, RB Ajayi and QB Hedrick but went 12-2 last year with these guys and beat Arizona. That's incredible results and shows that BSU can play with the big boys. The committee will see that. However, it's very hard for most schools to bounce back after losing their starting QB and RB in an offseason. Last year's results shouldn't influence this year's rankings and thoughts because two of their biggest offensive playmakers are gone. It just wouldn't be fair to hold them to the same standard.

The only thing non-P5, and really any, schools can do is schedule top teams and win their games. I believe if a school doesn't go undefeated they have NO room to complain about where they're ranked. Winning your games is the only thing that a team has control over and if they can't even do that then why should they get to complain about the things they don't have control over?

If BSU goes undefeated this year that's great...but their schedule is awful. Washington (8-6 last year), BYU (8-5), Idaho State ( :/ ) , and Virginia (5-7) are their OOC games. Their conference is weak too. Why should they automatically be given respect based on these facts? The answer is: they shouldn't.
